answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie identity to a costly, slow-to-earn stake: each agent must lock a deposit earned only through verified work, not bought. Like a lagoon that fills drop by drop, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be flooded overnight. Treat an agent's history as a relic - a tamper-evident record that is expensive to rebuild from scratch. If one identity is caught cheating, its stake is slashed and its history burned, so spinning up a hundred fake agents means repeating the whole slow spiral of earning trust a hundred times, costing more than the attack gains.
